To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a new 3D fully anisotropic Maxwell solver with piecewise constant electrically and magnetally anisotropic media that is stable for all material parameters and that the averaged method is more accurate and only slightly increases the computational run-time compared to the non-averaged first order accurate method.

we have developed a fully anisotropic FDTD Maxwell solver that is stable, second order accurate, and can be used for arbitrary fully anisotropic Maxwell media with piecewise constant electrically and magnetical materials co-located at the primary computational cell.

we have developed a new stable 3D FTD Maxwell's equations for arbitrary electrically anisotropic and magnetically isotropic media, and arbitrary magnetically anisotropy and electrically isotropic media, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and analysis of a stable 3D FTD Maxwell solver that can handle arbitrary anisotropic media with piecewise constant electric permittivity and magnetic permeability.
the numerical solution of the anisotropic Maxwell’s equations in 3D.
the development of the first stable 3D FDTM solver for arbitrary fully anisotropic Maxwell equations, which is applicable for a wide class of problems.

for the standard FDTD method the averaged method provides a significant improvement in accuracy with a negligible increase in computational cost.
the averaged method is a stable second order FDTD Maxwell solver with a 20\% increase in computational cost over the first order non-averaged solver.
the new averaged method is a second order accurate, fully anisotropic FDTD Maxwell solver that is stable, accurate, and robust.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the new averaged method is second-order accurate and stable for arbitrary anisotropic Maxwell media with co-located materials.
we have developed a stable, accurate, and robust FDTD method for Maxwell's equations for piecewise constant fully anisotropic electric and magnetic materials.
we have developed a stable, accurate and computationally efficient 3D FDT Maxwell solver for arbitrary fully anisotropic media.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the FDTD method for the arbitrary anisotropic Maxwell equations can be made stable, accurate, and computationally efficient.
the new method is accurate and stable for arbitrary fully anisotropic media.

the averaged method can be used to obtain second order accurate Maxwell solutions for arbitrary anisotropic media, and the non-averaged first order accurate method is sufficient for most applications.
